messages.subject: PC-prior paper, BYM model part
parts:
Dear INLA users, 

I have a question regarding the paper, ``Penalising model component complexity: A principled, practical approach to constructing priors’’ . The paper is given in the link below

 

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1403.4630.pdf

 

The question is regarding the statement:

 

``The independent random effects v are somehow partially included in the spatial random effect u for the case where no spatial dependence is found.’’

 

How does the new parametrization take this into account? I thought phi=1 meant all spatial variation and no unstructured component? How can one of the effects be partially included in the other? In BYM2 you have two independent effects where phi controls the amount of spatial effect and a common precision parameter. I do not see how one is contained in the other?


Best regards


Fredrik

messages.author: c421bf0e5f229fd1
messages.subject: Re: PC-prior paper, BYM model part
parts:
Here is my intuition, that might be wrong. Please correct do correct me if I am wrong:


Phi controls how much of each effect there is. If there is to be much spatial variation, then the contribution from the nonspatial effect needs to be small. We blend two types of effects together with the same typical marginal variance. In the one end we have only spatial variation with typical marginal variance 1 and in the other end only non-spatial variation with marginal variance 1. We therefore assign the same precision parameter on each effect. If we assigned independent priors on the precision parameters when considering each effect separately, then the priors can take values independently of each other. You do not take into account that one should be ``small’’ if the other effect is to be ``large’’ in the model. This is similar to specifying an independent Gaussian random model when the effect should have been a spatial random field model (but not the same of course).
